title: Second charge: Le Blanc calumniates Rome for stating what is truly Reformed consensus
source_text: CXXVIII. Nec difficilius est alterum crimen eluere quod mihi impingit vir Doctus. Nempe, si ipsi creditur, ego non tantum dissimulo quae sit vera Scholae Reformatae doctrina, ut ejus loco substituam, opinionem quandam novitiam & privatam, ultimis hisce demum annis, a duobus vel tribus obscuri nominis inter Reformatos hominibus admissam & probatam: Sed ulterius in mea dissimulatione pergens, audeo calumniae accusare Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae, quod eam dicant esse Reformatorum communem sententiam, quae revera talis est.
pass_a_gloss: Nor is it harder to wipe off the other crime the Learned Man fixes on me. Namely, if he is believed, I not only disguise what the true doctrine of the Reformed School is, so as to substitute in its place a certain novel and private opinion admitted and approved only in these last years by two or three men of obscure name among the Reformed: But going further in my dissimulation, I dare accuse the Doctors of the Roman Church of calumny because they say that is the Reformers' common opinion which in truth is such.
pass_b_english: Second charge: not only do I hide true Reformed doctrine under a novel private opinion, but I falsely brand Rome as calumnious for stating what really is Reformed consensus.
Le Blanc will answer this calumny charge next from his own opening thesis.

lemmas.gloss: to wipe off the other crime
to accuse the Doctors of the Roman Church of calumny

choices.why: Sets up CXXIX–CXXX defense of Thesis I.
rejected: concede Rome stated Reformed consensus truly
